citation.authors: Genovese G, Friedman DJ, Ross MD, Lecordier L et al

cited_by.title: Kidney disease, the APOL1 gene and the eGFR race adjustment

record.population: African Americans with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) and hypertension-attributed end-stage kidney disease (H-ESKD), and controls
record.design: Genetic association study with lab assays of the APOL1 protein
record.finding: Two independent APOL1 sequence variants were associated with FSGS (odds ratio 10.5, 95% CI 6.0-18.4) and H-ESKD (odds ratio 7.3, 95% CI 5.6-9.5). The variants are common in African chromosomes but absent from European chromosomes, and sit within haplotypes showing positive selection. Only the kidney-disease variants lysed Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense in vitro; the authors speculate a survival factor against sleeping sickness may have contributed to high kidney disease rates.
record.note: Odds ratios refer to carrying two risk variants against none in African Americans; the abstract does not give how common two-variant carriers are.
